turn_text: Let's put right now we are joined by U.S. Senator Tina Smith from Minnesota. Senator, good morning. Thank you so much for joining us.
Well, good morning, Jeff. It's great to be with you this morning.
How is life in Washington these days? Are you getting spring-like weather there? We're finally getting some spring here, so we feel pretty good about that.

Well, I'm calling in from my apartment in Washington, D.C. this morning, and I can tell you that the magnolia trees are starting to bloom in Washington, and there's a little bit of a haze of green and some of the trees. So the spring here comes a little quicker than our spring in Minnesota comes. But we are about to head back to Minnesota for a couple of weeks while the Senate won't be in session. We'll be working from back in Minnesota. So I'm really looking forward to getting
back.

Alright, let's talk about this bill that you have some legislation that you wish to put in. You've been working with also with Senator Klobuchar. It concerns adding fire sprinkler systems to public housing. And if our listeners will recall a couple of years ago, there was a tragic incident at Cedar High Apartments. And this bill, this is not the first time you've been working on this, though.

You're right. This is yesterday, Senator Klobuchar and I reintroduced this bill. We first wrote it in response to the terrible tragedy in the Cedar High Apartments, as you mentioned, which is an apartment complex in Minneapolis. Five lives were lost in this fire. And the tragedy is that in this public apartment building, there was no sprinkler system. So people were just trapped there. And Senator Klobuchar and I went to work on this, and we introduced legislation that would help to retrofit these buildings with sprinkler systems, the older apartment buildings. And I guess there are over 100 and 40 of them in Minnesota that were built before there was a requirement to have sprinklers are just not up to par. It's not acceptable that people would be living in unsafe conditions.
And you know,

a lot of the folks that live in these apartment buildings are elders and people living with disabilities. So they are at particular risk. I'm very hopeful that we're going to be able to get this passed. We worked on it last year. And I've actually spoken directly with the new Secretary of Housing and Urban Development, Marcia Fudge, to urge her to have this be a priority in the Biden-Harris budget this year. So we're going to work hard to get it done. It needs to get done.
Now, I understand there are some dollars attached to this, some grant money attached to this as well.

Yes, that's right. There are about $25 million that would be available each year and public housing authorities like we have all over Minnesota would be able to apply for these dollars to use them for retrofitting their buildings for sprinklers. These public apartment buildings are sadly in states of disrepair everywhere. There's just been a lack of investment in keeping them up to par and keeping them really livable. And so this would be very similar to what we are doing right now already to help to make sure that we're getting lead paint and other dangerous substances out of these apartment buildings. So we know that this kind of approach works and other circumstances where these buildings need to be improved. And I think that this is a good strategy. And it gives local housing authorities the tools that they need. And also, I think works really well with the efforts underway at the state legislature. to help fix this problem also.

Now, this is a problem. I'm sure is not unique to Minnesota. I would imagine there's older apartment buildings throughout the United States that has that. Have you been able to get some bipartisan support on this? Is everyone getting on board?

Well, you're right. This is not just a Minnesota issue. We see it everywhere. We don't yet have any bipartisan support for this legislation, but I do think that it is a bipartisan idea and the kind of thing that folks, whether they no matter where they live in the country should really appreciate the benefits of. So we're going to continue to push on it. And I hope as I said that we can get it included in the bigger budget bills that we'll all be considering later in the year.
Yeah, that's I guess was my next question is when does this actually happen? It's in a larger bill and that hopefully will be sometime later on this year.

Yep, what I hope will happen is that we will get it included and there's a variety of ways that we could get this done. One is as we take up a big infrastructure bill which we're working on already to improve that bill. People think about that big infrastructure bill we want to do is about roads and bridges and broadband and that's all really important and we'll be pushing that as hard as we can. But it also could include these kinds of maintenance improvements for public apartment buildings. So that's one idea. The other idea that we're looking at and working on is trying to get it included in the and big budget bills that will pass closer to the end of the year.
All right, Senator Smith, I know your time is valuable and limited, but is there anything else you'd like to add to this?
Nope, I want to just say thanks so much. It's great to speak with you, and I hope to talk to you soon.
All right, thank you very much for joining us. We certainly appreciate it. Enjoy your timing, dear. Last day in Washington, and welcome back to Minnesota.
Thank you so
much. Thank you. Alright.
Tina Smith, a U.S. Senator from Minnesota. You're listening to 95.1 FM AM 1080 KYMN Northfield.
